neighbours.label: In narrative about ancient, classical or biblical history, the word right before a period or regional-era name is due (Until ⟦the⟧ nineteenth century, in ⟦southern⟧ Italy, the Ion⟦ian⟧ school); output promotes ' century', ' modern', ' Renaissance'
fire: The Greek text of the gospels was copied by monks, yet a critical edition did not appear until the sixteenth century.
Aristotle's works on logic were lost to Latin readers and were not recovered until the twelfth century.
The philosopher Parmenides was born at Elea, a Greek colony in southern Italy, around 515 BCE.
The Epic of Gilgamesh lay buried in the ruins of Nineveh and was unknown to scholars before the Victorian era.
Egyptian hieroglyphs could not be read by anyone from late antiquity until the early 1820s.
The Etruscans ruled much of central Italy before Rome, and their tombs were first excavated in the eighteenth century.
Stoic philosophy began in Athens with Zeno and remained influential in Rome until the third century.
The codex of the Hebrew prophets was kept at Aleppo and was studied by few outsiders before the modern period.
quiet: The recipe for the sauce was copied by friends, yet a printed version did not appear until the following spring.

The goalkeeper was born at a small hospital in southern Ohio, and he still lives nearby.
The bicycle lay buried in the back of the garage and was unknown to the children before the house move.
